title: Qwen streamed-expert layer-major A/B measurements
methodology: bench/layer_major_ab.py generated deterministic exact-token prompts, alternated arms with reversed order in round 2, and compared generated token IDs. The OS file cache was not cleared. Peak memory values are sampled while the process runs.
notes: The 4K/8K post-gate case is one matched round; the layer-major arm explicitly fell back at both lengths.
The exact-minimum 16K active case is two matched rounds with reversed arm order.
The 32K active case is two matched rounds.
The three pre-gate 8K active attempts record the continuation divergence used to add the 16,384-token gate; cache/target variants are shown separately.
The report stores structured raw measurements from the harness; full model logs are not included because they contain full tokenized prompts.
A 16,383-token boundary case immediately below the 16,384-token minimum also fell back with exact eight-token parity.

A fresh two-round 16K run on revision 9b17dc454fd53e4df12259272ab4872df95b69a5 rebuilt the current checkout before execution. The active layer-major arm matched all eight generated IDs in both rounds; per-round prompt throughput was 553.62 and 552.37 tok/s versus 395.46 and 462.69 tok/s automatic, with 102274.4 MB versus 200688.6 MB reported H2D in each arm.

A fresh current-revision 8K run used --adapt-every 0 and --allow-fallback. Its first automatic and fallback arms returned different eight-token IDs although both exited successfully and the layer-major arm explicitly fell back with reason "a short prompt". Two subsequent automatic-only controls and two feature-flag fallback controls, using the same prompt token file and settings, all returned [248068, 198, 760, 1156, 6587, 728, 310, 59987]. Treat this A/B pair as inconclusive and do not infer that the feature flag caused the difference; this prompt exhibits output sensitivity across separate runs.

A second current-revision 16K A/B used docs/DETAILS.md as a distinct UTF-8 prompt body (SHA-256 fd904fa30298992cd2c50628310c23d8e48e50a6ff629f3bcb0bcd181d1e14d7). Layer-major was active in both reversed-order rounds and matched all eight generated token IDs. The harness HEAD was 8d9e2a8085772aa7c5a551789e0d289dff329398; the engine binary was built from 9b17dc454fd53e4df12259272ab4872df95b69a5.

Four 16K checks at 500 expert-cache slots used docs/DETAILS.md and the same exact token prompt (SHA-256 e577659a074388da8746f7b3173ddb056282db2d5ca2f7ac95aab8e8489c5ad7). The layer-major arm produced a different eight-token continuation in every check: automatic began [248068, 198, ...], layer-major began [248068, 271, ...]. This held with host and VRAM residual placement, frozen adaptive tiering, and a 4096-token super-chunk override. At 4096 grouping, reported H2D was 177330.9 MB versus 543615.2 MB, but parity still failed. These are correctness diagnostics, not performance claims; the 16K eligibility gate does not guarantee parity at a 500-slot cache.

One-round current-binary cache-capacity controls at 625 and 750 slots also matched all eight output IDs between automatic and layer-major on the same docs/DETAILS.md token prompt. Both produced [248068, 271, 248069, 271, 2495, 450, 369, 264], consistent with the existing two-round 1000-slot retest. At 500 slots, automatic itself instead produced [248068, 198, 760, 1156, 6587, 728, 310, 59987]. These single-round controls are not enough to define a safe minimum cache setting; they show that this prompt's continuation changes with cache-capacity execution paths and that the layer-major mismatch observed at 500 slots is meaningful.

cases.output_parity: all eight greedy output IDs matched in both reversed-order rounds

inconclusive: the first matched pair differed despite explicit short-prompt fallback; two later automatic-only controls and two later feature-flag fallback controls all produced the same alternate eight-token continuation
all eight generated token IDs matched in both active reversed-order rounds

runtime.cpu: Intel Core i5-14600K (14 cores, 20 logical processors)

divergence_diagnostic.capture: Temporary per-window FP32 logit instrumentation in the isolated pre-guard checkout; not part of the submitted branch. A separate --spec-follow run with --adapt-every 0 recorded final-residual hashes.
divergence_diagnostic.interpretation: The output changes because the second-token decision is a close near-tie after the prompt-derived residual state already differs. The measurements identify where the greedy continuation flips, but do not establish whether the upstream cause is changed expert accumulation, recurrent-state progression, or another numerical effect.
